content.text:
The drawing shows a 1,2,4-oxadiazole ring with a thiophene on one side and a nitrophenyl group on the other.

**Oxadiazole ring.** Going around the ring: O at the top, then N (upper right), then C (right, bearing the aryl group), then N (bottom), then C (left, bearing the thiophene), and back to O. So O1 is bonded to N2 and C5; N2 is bonded to C3; C3 is bonded to N4; N4 is bonded to C5. C3 carries the nitrophenyl group and C5 carries the thiophene, which makes this a 3-aryl-5-thienyl-1,2,4-oxadiazole.

**Thiophene.** It is attached at its 2-position, next to S.

**Nitrophenyl.** The benzene ring is attached to C3 of the oxadiazole. Numbering from that attachment carbon, the nitro group sits at the 3-position (meta). The "NO2" label has a stray dot above it, which I read as an artifact of the drawing and treat as an ordinary neutral nitro group.

SMILES for the oxadiazole core: c1(-c2cccs2)onc(n1)-c1cccc(c1)[N+](=O)[O-]

Checking the ring closure: c1(...)o n c(...) n1 gives C5, O1, N2, C3, N4 and back to C5, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: [O-][N+](=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1noc(n1)-c1cccs1
